_comment: Single source of truth for every ontology used across the pipeline.
Read from bash via toxvaldb/config/ontologies.sh and from Python via
toxvaldb/config/ontology_config.py.
'local_dir' is where the local snapshots live, relative to toxvaldb/
(TOXVALDB_ROOT in the job scripts).
'exclude_uris' (optional) lists classes left out of the prepared tree, with every
descendant reachable only through them. Classification names one column per
label, so it is how an ontology that labels two live classes identically is made
to work; 'exclude_note' records why each exclusion was made.
'db_dir' is where this ontology's generated DBs live, relative to the
02.prepare_ontologies module root. every ontology added after the freeze uses 'outputs_local'
because the shared 'outputs' symlink is not writable by us (issue #5); when
write access lands, set it to 'outputs' here and nothing else changes.
local_sha256 is verified on every resolve. The snapshots are gitignored (~0.5GB),
so the checksum is the only in-repo record of which bytes produced a result;
restore them with 02.prepare_ontologies/inputs/download_ontologies.sh.
'order' is every configured ontology, in the canonical order Slurm array
indices map onto. 'groups' names the subsets that individual jobs run:
all         every entry in 'order' -- implicit, never listed here, so a new
ontology joins evaluation automatically by being added to 'order'
guidelines  the original five. Guideline runs deliberately exclude ontologies
added later, so a new ontology enters this group only if named.
Jobs select a group rather than carrying their own list; that is what keeps the
subsets from drifting apart across scripts. Adding an ontology still means
bumping '#SBATCH --array' in the jobs for its groups -- Slurm parses that
directive before the script runs, so it cannot come from here; ontology_by_index
warns when the range and the group disagree.
SOURCE POLICY ('pin', per ontology):
pin=local  Frozen. The published results were produced from this exact snapshot,
so it stays the source until someone deliberately refreshes it.
pin=url    Tracks the canonical URL. Used for ontologies added after the freeze.
Every entry carries BOTH a local snapshot and (where one exists) a url, so either
can be selected. Override the policy globally with ONTOLOGY_SOURCE=local|url; that
is the deliberate-refresh path, not something a results run should do.
rdflib cannot infer a serialization for OBO purls -- they redirect to GitHub release
assets served as application/octet-stream -- so every source carries an explicit
format that must be passed to every script that parses it.
Pinned release URLs resolve for hp, mp, mondo, symp, doid, oae, nbo and pato; each is pinned to the exact release
its snapshot holds. uberon, txpo, mpath and cmo declare a versionIRI whose path 404s, so
they track latest and cannot be pinned. aop and hpath have no url at all.

aop.note: AOP-Wiki ontology (<http://aopwiki.org/ontology>), not an OBO ontology. obo/aop.owl 404s and there is no other stable download, so this one is local-only and can never be refreshed from a url.

hp.note: Snapshot and url are both hp-international 2026-02-16, so ONTOLOGY_SOURCE=url yields the same release. root_uri is HP_0000001 ('All') for hierarchy traversal, while root_term is the deeper 'phenotypic abnormality' used for depth. They are deliberately different.

hpath.note: Declares the placeholder IRI obo/TEMP over an MC_ term namespace: a hand-built extract with no published release. Local-only and unrefreshable.

mp.note: Snapshot and url are both mp-international 2026-01-27, so ONTOLOGY_SOURCE=url yields the same release. Newer releases exist (2026-08-25 at time of writing); bump the url and local_sha256 together and rebuild mp.db if you take one.

txpo.release_seen: local snapshot 2026-04-24; a 74KB extract that declares no versionIRI
txpo.note: The snapshot is a 74KB extract; the full release behind the url is ~18MB. txpo.db was built from the extract, so switching to the url without rebuilding the DB would make the graph and the DB disagree. Refresh both together or neither. The url declares versionIRI .../releases/2022-12-07/txpo.owl but that path 404s, so it cannot be pinned.

uberon.note: basic.owl, not the full uberon.owl. Added after the freeze, so it tracks the url. The snapshot is the 2026-06-19 release that built uberon.db; set ONTOLOGY_SOURCE=local to reproduce that run exactly, since the url tracks latest and will move.

mondo.note: mondo-simple.owl, not the full mondo.owl: the simple product carries the MONDO classes and their is-a hierarchy without the external axioms this pipeline never traverses. 36,089 classes, 36,015 of them labelled, 31,558 in the subtree rooted at MONDO_0000001 'disease'. Snapshot and url are both the 2026-09-01 release, so ONTOLOGY_SOURCE=url yields the same bytes.

symp.note: By far the smallest ontology configured here: 1,020 classes, all labelled, of which 125 are obsolete and the other 895 form the subtree rooted at SYMP_0000462 'symptom' -- the obsolete ones are exactly the classes left without a named superclass. Snapshot and url are both the 2026-07-30 release, so ONTOLOGY_SOURCE=url yields the same bytes. Covers patient-reported symptoms and clinical signs, so it complements hp (clinical phenotypic abnormalities) and mondo (named diseases) rather than overlapping them.

mpath.exclude_note: MPATH labels two live branches identically: 'plasmacytosis' is both MPATH_852 (under MPATH_194 'immune mediated disease') and MPATH_874 (under MPATH_602 'hyperplastic tissue'), each with 'systemic' and 'cutaneous' children (853/854 and 876/875). Classification names one output column per label, so the duplicates crash it (job 53687834, 2026-09-22). The 852 branch is dropped; the 874 branch is kept because its definition ('a hyperplastic condition') matches its parent. That leaves 836 classes.
mpath.note: URL-only: no local snapshot is kept, so ONTOLOGY_SOURCE=local cannot resolve it. The declared versionIRI (obo/mpath/2020-05-19/mpath.owl) 404s, so it cannot be pinned, but MPATH has not been released since 2020 so latest is stable in practice. 891 classes, 890 labelled, 50 obsolete. The top class is MPATH_1000 'pathological phenotype observation', a wrapper whose only children are MPATH_458 'normal' and MPATH_0 'pathological entity'; rooting at MPATH_0 keeps 'normal' out of the candidate terms. 839 classes in the subtree rooted at MPATH_0. Mouse histopathology (lesions and pathological processes), so it overlaps hpath in scope but is the published OBO counterpart rather than a hand-built extract.

cmo.note: URL-only: no local snapshot is kept. The declared versionIRI (obo/cmo/releases/2026-09-19/cmo.owl) 404s, so it cannot be pinned and tracks latest; CMO releases often, so record the versionIRI each run logs. ~9.6MB. 4,199 classes, all labelled, 67 obsolete, 4,042 in the subtree rooted at CMO_0000000 'clinical measurement'. The other 93 live classes (mostly regional brain RNA levels) are attached only by part_of, not is-a, so they fall outside the traversed tree. Covers measurements (organ weights, blood chemistry, body morphology), so it complements the phenotype and disease ontologies for the many ToxValDB effects that are reported as a measured change.

doid.note: URL-only: no local snapshot is kept, but the url is pinned to the 2026-08-31 release, which is byte-identical to obo/doid.owl as of 2026-09-22. ~28.6MB. 14,797 classes, all labelled, 2,515 obsolete; the other 12,282 form the subtree rooted at DOID_4 'disease'. Overlaps mondo, which integrates DOID; it is kept as a separate, human-disease-curated alternative rather than a complement.

oae.note: URL-only: no local snapshot is kept, but the url is pinned to the 2026-04-15 release, which is byte-identical to obo/oae.owl as of 2026-09-29. ~11.9MB. 10,595 classes, 120 obsolete; 89% of the live classes are OAE's own, the rest imported (mostly UBERON). OAE_0000001 'adverse event' has 8,992 descendants, all OAE, all labelled, 8,638 with a definition, organised by organ system (cardiovascular, neurological, immune, skin, digestive, abnormal investigation result...). Every label ends in 'AE'. Complements the phenotype and disease ontologies with clinical adverse-event terms, including CTCAE-style graded ones ('Grade 3 edema trunk AE'). Two pairs of classes differ only in case -- 'VIIth nerve paralysis AE' (OAE_0000655) and 'viith nerve paralysis AE' (OAE_0004734), 'Miller Fisher syndrome AE' (OAE_0002064) and 'miller fisher syndrome AE' (OAE_0009166) -- and are left in: output columns are case-sensitive, so unlike mpath's duplicates they do not crash classification. Like most ontologies here, a few labels (e.g. the two pairs above, 'injection site abscess AE') still collide once sanitize_name lowercases and strips punctuation.

nbo.note: URL-only: no local snapshot is kept, but the url is pinned to the 2023-07-04 release, which is byte-identical to obo/nbo.owl as of 2026-09-29; NBO has not been released since. ~5.6MB. 4,546 classes but only 932 are NBO's own; the rest are imported UBERON, GO, CHEBI and NCBITaxon. NBO's own classes form two separate branches: NBO_0000243 'behavioral phenotype' (296 descendants: seizures, mood and psychotic disorders, abnormal kinesthetic, feeding, rhythmic behaviour...) and NBO_0000313 'behavior process' (634 descendants: normal behaviours such as locomotion, learning, social behaviour). Rooted at the phenotype branch because ToxValDB effects are abnormal findings, like hp and mp; the process branch is the alternative, and it would need 'predator avoidance behavior' de-duplicated (NBO_0000471 and NBO_0015001). The smallest subtree configured here after symp.

pato.note: URL-only: no local snapshot is kept, but the url is pinned to the 2025-05-14 release, which is byte-identical to obo/pato.owl as of 2026-09-29. ~21.1MB. 8,625 classes, 982 obsolete; only 1,887 of the live ones are PATO's own, the rest imported GO, UBERON, CL and CHEBI. PATO_0000001 'quality' has 1,888 descendants (1,886 PATO, 2 PCO), all labelled, 1,873 with a definition. PATO is the quality half of the entity-quality definitions behind hp and mp, so its terms carry no entity ('decreased mass density', 'flat', 'increased thickness'): findings can only be classified by the kind of change, not by what changed. A handful of labels ('aerobic', 'sessile', 'deciduous'...) collide once sanitize_name lowercases and strips punctuation; exact labels are unique, so classification does not crash.
